comparison: §VII-C RQ3 ablation, Table IV: full ACFix vs 'W/o ACG' (token costs in Table VI, §VII-F)
model_config: Same in both arms: GPT-4-0613 generator + validator (MAD), RBAC taxonomy, static grammar checks; temperature 0, max 4096 output tokens
dataset_metric: 118-case AC vulnerability benchmark; repair success rate (fixed/118)
budget_control: Not explicitly capped, but the structured arm is shorter: Table VI avg tokens ACFix 1,956.35 vs W/o ACG 2,813.68 ('W/o ACG consumed more tokens than ACFix because the raw source code was not processed')
arm_a: Full ACFix: serialized AC Context Graph (interprocedural slice over PDG + call graph, with edges described in NL) supplied to GPT-4
arm_b: W/o ACG: same pipeline, raw contract source code supplied in place of the ACG
other_changes: none reported ('W/o ACG has the same implementation as ACFix but without ACG'); note 5 contracts exceeded the token limit in W/o ACG (patches generated for 113/118), counted as failures
delta: 106 vs 112 of 118 fixed: 89.83% vs 94.92% (-5.09 pp); paper: 'ACG contributed to 12 more successful cases' (Answer to RQ3)
rationale: 'W/o ACG has the same implementation as ACFix but without ACG', and W/o ACG instead incorporates 'the raw source code of contracts' in the prompt, so only the code context supplied to the same GPT-4 pipeline changes. The structured arm is shorter (Table VI: 1,956 vs 2,814 avg tokens). Caveat: up to 5 of the 6 lost cases may stem from token-limit overflow in the raw-code arm (113 vs 118 patches generated), so part of the gain is context-length feasibility rather than representation quality. Also, the paper's 'additional 12 cases' conflicts with its own Table IV (112-106 = 6).

comparison: §5.1 RQ3, Table 4: Vul-RAG (knowledge-level RAG) vs code-level RAG baseline, per LLM
model_config: Same LLM per row (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 3.5, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, DeepSeek); the knowledge base is built offline with GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 (Vul-RAG arm only)
dataset_metric: PairVul (586 Linux-kernel vulnerable/patched pairs, top-10 CWEs); pair accuracy (also balanced recall/precision)
budget_control: Not reported; no token accounting for either arm
arm_a: Vul-RAG: top-10 LLM-extracted, abstracted knowledge items (functional semantics, causes, fixing solutions) retrieved by code + abstract purpose + detailed behavior queries (BM25 + RRF re-ranking), then checked iteratively one item per prompt
arm_b: Code-level RAG: similar code snippets retrieved by code similarity from the training set and added to the prompt (Fig. 5(b))
other_changes: Retrieval stage differs (LLM-generated semantic queries, three-query BM25 + RRF vs code-only retrieval, so different items are retrieved); inference paradigm differs (iterative per-knowledge-item checking with early stop vs single augmented prompt); an extra LLM (GPT-3.5) builds the knowledge base
delta: Pair accuracy, code RAG -> Vul-RAG: GPT-4o 0.05->0.32, Claude 0.11->0.27, Qwen 0.09->0.26, DeepSeek 0.05->0.30 (+16 to +27 points absolute; Table 4)
rationale: The authors attribute the gain to two sources: '(1) In the retrieval phase, knowledge-level RAG more accurately retrieves semantically relevant vulnerabilities ... (2) In the inference phase ... the high-level representation'. The retrieval stage and the iterative detection loop both change along with the representation. No same-retrieval comparison isolates the representation alone.

comparison: §V-B RQ2, Table IV: CGP-Tuning vs 'CGP-Tuning w/o cross-modal alignment' (also checked: Table III, Prompt Tuning vs CGP-Tuning)
model_config: Same frozen backbone in each pair (CodeLlama, CodeGemma, Qwen2.5-Coder, 7B); separately trained adapters with different architectures; same optimizer/LR/1 epoch, 32 soft prompt embeddings
dataset_metric: DiverseVul (under-sampled); accuracy (also P/R/F1). The Table IV CGP-Tuning row (0.6627 CodeLlama) differs from Table III (0.6582), and the split used for Table IV is not stated
budget_control: Soft-prompt budget fixed at 32 embeddings in both arms; text input identical; max 16,000 tokens at test
arm_a: Full CGP-Tuning: CPG (Joern) -> type-aware + positional embeddings -> GAT -> multi-head cross-attention + projector -> 32 graph-enhanced soft prompts + code text
arm_b: W/o cross-modal alignment: skips step 10 and 'uses the soft prompt embeddings at step 2 directly' (graph features no longer reach the LLM) + code text
other_changes: Trained adapter architecture and parameter count differ (alignment module, i.e. attention + projector, removed); each arm is a separately trained model
delta: Accuracy 0.6627->0.4752 (CodeLlama, -18.75 pp), 0.6154->0.4700 (CodeGemma, -14.54 pp), 0.6572->0.5123 (Qwen, -14.49 pp); paper: 'accuracy drops of approximately 19, 15, and 14 percentage points' (Table IV)
rationale: The ablated arm is a different trained model: removing the alignment module changes the learned adapter's architecture, not just the input ('plain soft prompt embeddings cannot bridge the semantic gap ... without the multi-head attention mechanism, nor ... without the projection'). The closest representation contrast, Prompt Tuning vs CGP-Tuning in Table III (equal 32-embedding budget, same hyperparameters; accuracy 0.5901->0.6582 CodeLlama, 0.5113->0.6219 CodeGemma, 0.5758->0.6507 Qwen), also adds a trainable graph encoder, so it is not R-strict either. The arm without alignment (0.4752) also scores below plain Prompt Tuning (0.5901), which points to an optimization artifact rather than the value of the CPG.

comparison: §4.1 RQ1, Table 1: LLM4PFA vs LLM4SA (and LLMDFA), NPD; also §4.4 Table 4: LLM4PFA vs NoContext / BatchSol
model_config: GPT-4o-mini backbone, temperature 0, in all arms
dataset_metric: SAFP-Bench-C (Linux kernel, OpenSSL, Libav); FPR_R (false-positive reduction recall), also Acc/FPR_P/Pre/Recall
arm_a: LLM4PFA: agent-driven iterative, self-planned context retrieval along the path + LLM-extracted path constraints solved iteratively with an SMT solver
arm_b: LLM4SA: single prompt with the code snippet + bug report (public implementation); LLMDFA: dataflow summarization + Z3 path validation script synthesis
other_changes: Analysis algorithm and pipeline differ: agent tool loop for context retrieval and SMT constraint solving (symbolic verification) in LLM4PFA vs a single prompt in LLM4SA. The §4.4 ablations remove the agent context-analysis loop (NoContext) or the iterative solving (BatchSol), both pipeline components
delta: NPD FPR_R: LLM4SA 0.51 -> LLM4PFA 0.72; LLMDFA 0.35 -> 0.72; paper: 'FPR_R improvement of 41.1% - 105.7%' (relative). Ablation: '136.7% - 173.1% improvements in FPR_R' over NoContext/BatchSol (Total FPR_R 0.71 vs 0.26/0.30)
rationale: Same model and dataset, but the arms differ in a full pipeline: an agent tool loop and SMT-based constraint solving vs LLM4SA's single 'code snippet and the bug report' prompt. The §4.4 variants also remove components ('NoContext performs symbolic range reasoning without iterative context analysis driven by the LLM agent'). No comparison in the paper varies only the representation.

comparison: Appendix C: LLMxCPG-D on CPG slices vs the same LLMxCPG-D on full code (slicing step bypassed)
model_config: Same fine-tuned LLMxCPG-D (QwQ-32B-Preview + LoRA, reduced Yes/No classification head) in both arms; note LLMxCPG-D was fine-tuned on slices only (§3, 'fine-tuning dataset for classifying code slices')
dataset_metric: FormAI-v2, PrimeVul, SVEN test sets; ACCURACY (not F1, as the record states)
budget_control: Not explicitly capped; the structured arm is shorter (slicing reduces code by 78.70% FormAI, 67.84% PrimeVul, 70.22% SVEN, §4.3.1)
arm_a: CPG slice extracted by LLMxCPG-Q-generated CPGQL queries run in Joern
other_changes: none in the model/inference path; the slice arm needs the upstream query-generation model + Joern to produce its input (the representation itself). Asymmetry: the classifier was trained only on slices, so the full-code arm is out of distribution
delta: Accuracy: FormAI 0.8146 vs 0.6762 (+13.84 pp), PrimeVul 0.7250 vs 0.4875 (+23.75 pp), SVEN 0.6020 vs 0.5078 (+9.42 pp) (Appendix C)
rationale: 'we evaluate LLMxCPG-D on the test datasets using the full code, bypassing the CPG slicing step': same model and metric, only the supplied code differs, and the slice arm is shorter. Caveats: (1) the record mislabels these as F1, but the paper reports accuracy; (2) LLMxCPG-D was fine-tuned on slices, so the train/test mismatch favours the slice arm and the gap is an upper bound on the representation effect.

comparison: §4.2.1 RQ1, Table 6 / Fig. 1 (original vs obfuscated code; virtualization and mixed-language attack success); §4.2.3 RQ3 (Table 13, QWEN-14B PrimeVul L1)
model_config: Same LLM and prompt per comparison (15 LLMs, temperature 1e-5); obfuscations generated by gpt-4o
dataset_metric: Smart-bugs, PrimeVul, ReposVul_cpp, ReposVul_py; detection success rate (type evaluation: score 3/4 positive) and downgrade/upgrade counts ('attack success rate'); RQ3 uses the relaxed existence evaluation
budget_control: Not reported/not controlled; transformations such as virtualization (interpreter/bytecode) and mixed-language (inline assembly / external call) change code length, and per-arm length is not reported
arm_b: LLM-obfuscated source code (layout / data-flow / control-flow / mixed-language transformation of the same raw text)
other_changes: none in the pipeline; the obfuscated input comes from a stochastic gpt-4o rewrite whose semantic preservation is not independently verified
delta: Virtualization 'attack success rate of up to approximately 80% on the C/C++ datasets'; mixed-language 'around 75%' (Finding #2). RQ3 existence evaluation: QWEN-14B PrimeVul 'jumps from 0.39 on the original code to 0.80 after applying L1 obfuscation'
rationale: Same model and prompt, and only the code text differs ('For each obfuscated sample, we compared the model's detection results against its unobfuscated counterpart'). Input length is not controlled or reported, and virtualization/mixed-language transforms add code, so the conservative rule applies. This is also a surface-form perturbation, not a structured representation, so it does not test structure vs text. The 0.39->0.80 example uses the relaxed existence criterion, under which 'obfuscation rarely reduces detection success'.

comparison: §5.3 RQ2, Table 4: full MalSkills vs w/o Symbolic Extractor / w/o Neuro Extractor / w/o Symbolic Reasoner / w/o Neuro Reasoner
model_config: gpt-5.3-codex-medium as default model in all LLM-using arms; the 'w/o Neuro Reasoner' arm removes the LLM from classification entirely
arm_a: Full pipeline: parsing-based symbolic SSO extractor + LLM neuro extractor -> Skill Dependency Graph -> symbolic + neural reasoning
arm_b: One stage removed: symbolic extractor (rule-based static analysis), neuro extractor (LLM), symbolic reasoner, or neuro reasoner (LLM)
other_changes: Each arm removes a pipeline component (static rule-based extractor or symbolic/neural reasoning stage), not just model input; 'w/o Neuro Reasoner' is classification without the LLM
delta: w/o Symbolic Extractor: recall 0.92->0.27, F1 0.93->0.43; w/o Neuro Reasoner: F1 0.93->0.71, FPR 0.05->0.49; w/o Neuro Extractor F1 0.93 (unchanged); w/o Symbolic Reasoner unchanged (Table 4)
rationale: The paper frames these as component ablations: 'To understand the contribution of each major component ... w/o Symbolic Extractor. This variant removes the symbolic extraction component and relies only on the neural extractor'. Removing a static-analysis extractor or a reasoning stage is a pipeline-component change, and the neuro-reasoner ablation drops the LLM itself.

comparison: §5.2 RQ2, Table 3: MemRepair Full (L1+L2+L3) vs Loop Only (and single-tier variants)
model_config: DeepSeek-v3.2 in all arms; same agent + Verifier feedback loop
budget_control: Not controlled; only per-task cost reported (Full $0.26 vs Loop Only $0.21)
arm_a: Full: hierarchical memory retrieval (L1 History-Fix, L2 Security-Pattern, L3 Refinement-Trajectory) feeding the agent and the Verifier
arm_b: Loop Only: 'disables all memory retrieval (L1-L3) and retains only the feedback-driven control logic in the Verifier' (coarse Relocate/Regenerate signals only)
other_changes: Memory module with its own retrieval stage added/removed; L3 also changes the Verifier's refinement guidance inside the loop ('L3 acts as a semantic filter and refinement engine during the feedback loop')
delta: 58.0% vs 36.0% resolved (+22.0 pp); L3 only 50.5%, L2 only 48.0%, L1 only 42.0% (Table 3)
rationale: The ablation adds/removes a memory module: 'The Loop Only variant disables all memory retrieval (L1-L3)'. That is a retrieval/memory component, not a representation swap. The closest representation contrast, L2 abstract patterns vs L1 raw historical snippets (48.0% vs 42.0%), still compares two different memory stores with their own retrieval, and budget is unreported, so it is not R-strict either.

comparison: §V RQ2, Table II: full AgenticRepair vs w/o Code-Structure / w/o Program-Execution / w/o Commit-History Context (strict mode)
model_config: gpt-5.2-2025-12-11, medium reasoning effort, temperature 1.0; analysis subagents max 20 steps, repair subagent max 75 steps; same multi-agent scaffold
dataset_metric: SEC-Bench 200 CVE-sourced instances; repair success rate (strict mode)
budget_control: Step caps only (20/75 steps); context/token budget not controlled or reported
arm_a: Full: three ReAct context-engineering subagents (code-structure via CodeQL etc., runtime via GDB/Valgrind, commit history) produce partial contexts synthesized into the repair subagent's episodic memory
arm_b: One facet removed: the corresponding context subagent and its partial context are absent
other_changes: Removing a facet removes an entire tool-using ReAct subagent (its tool loop and tools, e.g. CodeQL) and shortens the context; single run at temperature 1.0
delta: Strict success 75.0% (150) -> 73.5% (147) w/o code-structure (-1.5 pp), 74.5% (149) w/o execution (-0.5 pp), 73.0% (146) w/o commit-history (-2.0 pp) (Table II)
rationale: Each facet is produced by a separate ReAct subagent that 'selects and invokes domain-specific tools to gather its facet of information', so the ablation removes an agent tool-loop component, not only a representation. The deltas (1-4 of 200 instances, single run at temperature 1.0) are within run-to-run noise. Note: the record's structure_gain cites 73.0-74.5% for the facet ablations, but the code-structure arm is 73.5%.
